critiques.target: H4.1 (a) and H4.3: 'rebuild noise moves the 3-seed mean only about ±0.03 pp'
critiques.issue: Later results contradict this. Two math-identical rebuilds moved individual seeds by 0.1–0.44 pp. E036 vs E038 is the same commit: seed 0 +0.31, seed 1 −0.09, seed 2 −0.44. E035 vs E034 changed only prepare and was checked with torch.equal: seeds +0.16, +0.11, +0.01. The 3-seed mean then moved by 0.03–0.09 pp, but that comes from averaging small samples; it does not show the trajectory is preserved. E019's conclusion that the seeds 0–2 offset is a persistent seed×RNG-stream effect is therefore at best partly true. A max-autotune/cudagraph rebuild is a partial re-draw of the trajectory. So the 'E036 is feasible' record is one draw, and the next draw (E038, 0.7525) failed.
critiques.suggestion: Rewrite H4.1(a): per-seed rebuild noise is about 0.2–0.3 pp, and the 3-seed mean shift is under 0.1 pp in 4 observations. Lower H4.3's confidence that local results transfer to the judge. In the final report, say the tip passed the local bar on 1 of 2 builds (0.7532, then 0.7525). Do not present 5.31 s as reproducibly feasible. Do not re-run the commit until it passes; that would be cherry-picking.

critiques.target: E040 and E041 refutations (H2.3.6 extension, H4.2.5)
critiques.issue: Both arms were compared against E036's seeds 3–12 mean of 0.7557. E036 was kept because that number cleared the gate, so it carries the winner's curse. E038 measured E036 on fresh seeds 13–22 at 0.7538. Against that unbiased baseline, E041 is −0.01 pp, not −0.20, and passes H4.2.5's ≤0.1 pp rule. E040 is −0.09 pp, not −0.28. With an SE of the difference around 0.13 pp, neither result shows a loss. The notebook's mechanisms ('the 24 px bridge carries accuracy', 'early steps carry LR warm-up and peak') explain an effect that may not exist. The same bias applies to every comparison made against a just-kept tip's held-out mean: changes look worse than they are.
critiques.suggestion: Mark H4.2.5 and the 40/0/30/30 child as inconclusive, not refuted. From now on, compare against a baseline measured on seeds that were not used to select it: E036's seeds 13–22 (0.7538), or the pooled 20 seeds (0.7547) with a stated discount. Re-test E040+E041 stacked (about −5% time) on 20 seeds before writing either off.

critiques.target: Decision statistics in general (H4.1, H4.2's rate rankings, notebook exchange-rate claims)
critiques.issue: Most keep/discard and 'better/worse than the dial' calls rest on one 10-seed difference of 0.15–0.28 pp, which is about 1.1–2σ with SE of the difference 0.10–0.14 pp. Examples: E026 −0.15, E029 −0.05, E030 −0.24, E032 −0.23, E025 −0.27, E022 −0.24, E036 +0.08, E041 −0.20, E040 −0.28. H4.2 says 'rank dials only when intervals separate', yet the notebook does exactly that ranking: E041 '0.85 s/pp, worse than the dial', E031 '2.3 s/pp may beat it', E026 '1.2 s/pp'. Gates also changed between experiments: 0.7535 (E027), 0.752 (E033), 0.7545 (E034, E036), so the tip was assembled under inconsistent rules.
critiques.suggestion: Fix one gate, for example a 20-seed mean of at least 0.7545 on seeds not used for selection. Report every exchange rate with a CI. For any change worth under 0.25 pp, run 20 seeds per arm (about 5 min) before treating it as a refutation. Re-label the 'scalar is flat' conclusions (E009, E013, E014: 3 seeds only) as 'not detected'.

critiques.target: H6.3 and H6 regime (b): 'BN/GELU/pool on 31×31 maps are memory-bound'
critiques.issue: E039 contradicts the mechanism as stated. Its notebook places group-1 BN on 15×15 maps, which follows from the airbench conv→pool→BN→GELU order. Removing those BN reductions saved only 0.6%, within build noise. In the frozen step, the only 31×31 tensors are the first conv's output and the maxpool. E028's 27% saving for about 20% of MACs is equally well explained by inefficient conv kernels on the 24-channel whitening output: dgrad and wgrad with small Cin and K misaligned with tensor-core tiles. Group 1's backward is about 13% of step FLOPs, so it would only need to run at about half efficiency.
critiques.suggestion: Run the torch.profiler trace that H6.3.1, H6.1.1, H6.2.1 and H2.2.4 all call for. It is one diagnostic and none has been run in 41 experiments. If group-1 conv1 is the slow kernel, a new lever opens that speeds up every step, not just frozen ones: pad or widen the whitening output to 32 channels, or change group-1 conv1's layout or algorithm.

critiques.target: H6.2 (tile alignment) and H6.1 (small maps under-use tensor cores)
critiques.issue: Map-size arithmetic explains E024 without any tile-efficiency story. At 26 px the maps are 25/12/6/3, and at 28 px they are 27/13/6/3. Group 3, about 29% of MACs, runs at 6×6 in both, and group 2's later convs go from 13 to 12. So the expected saving is well below (26/28)², and the 'pixel model' was the wrong baseline. The 'off-grid' list is also incoherent: 23, 27 and 31 are just as odd as 25, and 320 channels is a multiple of 64, which is tile-aligned for fp16. E021's sublinear time fits E028's finding that group 1 takes more than its MAC share of time, which leaves less time in group 2 to cut. E021 therefore points away from H6.1: the big maps are slow, not the small ones.
critiques.suggestion: Model time by MACs per group at the actual post-pool map sizes before invoking kernel efficiency. Downgrade H6.2 and H6.1 unless the profiler shows per-layer TFLOP/s differences. Use the corrected model to choose resolutions whose post-pool maps actually shrink.

critiques.target: E037 / H2.6.4 interpretation ('group 1 still learns usefully at 60–75%')
critiques.issue: This is the most surprising result: freezing 25% of steps cost 0 pp (E028/E034), but freezing 40% cost 0.56 pp (still about 0.37 pp against the unbiased 0.7538 baseline). The nonlinearity has an unexamined explanation. The 32 px phase starts at 70%, so a 60% freeze means the stem never trains at 32 px, a FixRes-style train/test mismatch (H2.3 mechanism b). It is also confounded with a steeper group-1 LR anneal, from peak to 0 by 60%. H2.6.6 (does the anneal matter?) was never tested.
critiques.suggestion: Test a freeze at 70–72%, at or just after the 28→32 px switch, with the anneal ending at the freeze point. If it costs about 0, the cliff is the resolution switch, and freezing group 1 at 32 px soon after the switch is the right dose. Freezing at 65% or 68% would only map the curve. Also run H2.6.6, which is a cheap control for whether the E028 result depends on the anneal.

structured_output.summary:
The tip is E036 at 5.31 s, and it is probably not reliably feasible. Its seeds 3–12 mean (0.7557) was used to select it and is inflated: fresh seeds 13–22 give 0.7538, and a rebuild of the same commit (E038) gave 0.7525 on seeds 0–2, below the 0.753 bar. Rebuilds also re-draw individual seeds by 0.1–0.44 pp. That contradicts H4.1(a)'s '±0.03 pp' and E019's claim that the seeds 0–2 offset is persistent.

Measured against the unbiased baseline, the post-E036 refutations largely disappear. E041 goes from −0.20 to about −0.01 pp, and E040 from −0.28 to about −0.09 pp. Together they may have been a ~5% time saving that was thrown away. Most other keep/discard calls rest on single 10-seed differences of about 1–2σ, under keep gates that changed from experiment to experiment.

Two mechanisms look wrong:
- **H6.3** (memory-bound BN on 31×31 maps) is undercut by E039. Group-1 BN sits on 15×15 maps and removing it saved nothing. E028's saving is just as well explained by inefficient convs on the 24-channel whitening output.
- **H6.2** (tile alignment) is unnecessary. At 26 and 28 px, group 3 runs at 6×6 either way, which explains E024's small saving. E021 points to big maps being slow, not small ones.

E037 is the most surprising result: a 25% freeze cost nothing, but a 40% freeze cost about 0.4–0.56 pp. A likely cause is that a 60% freeze means the stem never trains at 32 px. A freeze at 70–72% would test this.

Never tried despite being flagged:
- BN-statistics recomputation, which is cheap, cuts variance, and was named after E005
- Any batch-size experiment (all of H5). E031, E033 and E041 hint that step count, not pixels, carries accuracy.
- Isolating Muon's contribution and its Newton-Schulz cost, including a code read that needs no run
- Plain EMA, LS 0.1, and narrowing group 1
- Any profiler trace, though four open Lvl3s depend on one

Many statuses also contradict their own evidence tokens, and the Lvl1 text still describes E027 as the tip.

Next steps:
1. Recompute BN statistics, judged on 20 fresh seeds.
2. Re-baseline, then re-test E040 and E041 stacked.
3. Run one profiler trace.
4. Test the freeze at 70%.
5. Run the H5 batch tests.
